bull_bear.body: Debt used temporarily for Thailand equity infusion (repaid); Intangible asset build-up from BBK consolidation; Focus on organic store expansion (200-225 stores).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Gas supply volatility; Commodity inflation (coffee/cocoa); Pizza Hut turnaround execution risk; Macro demand sustainability; Merger regulatory approval delays (CCI).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on KFC revival and merger timeline; Pragmatic on macro uncertainties; Transformational regarding new leadership (CTO, CMO, COO) and 'DIL 2.0' strategy.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Strategic decoupling of online vs. offline pricing/promotions to drive dine-in traffic (offline gains > online losses); Discontinuation of 'Tea Live' brand after testing; Shift to electrical cooking equipment in BBK to hedge gas risk; Temporary debt spike was specifically for Thailand equity, not operational stress.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: KFC: Rev 586 Cr (+15% YoY), SSSG +4.9%, Brand Contrib Margin 17.0%; Pizza Hut: SSSG -3.7% (sequential improvement), Brand Contrib slightly negative; Own Brands (Vaango/BBK): Mid-single digit positive SSSG, BBK turned profitable; International: Rev >500 Cr (+20% YoY), Brand Contrib Margin 17.7%; Franchise (Costa): Rev +3% YoY, GM down 1.2% due to commodity costs.

business.body:
- "Devyani International Limited is one of India's largest chain quick service restaurant (QSR) operators, with a network of over 2,200 stores across more than 350 cities in India, Thailand, Nigeria, and Nepal."
- "DIL holds the distinction of being the largest franchisee of Yum! Brands in India and Nepal. In addition, DIL is the sole franchisee in India for several international brands, including Costa Coffee, New York Fries, and Sanook Kitchen."
- Portfolio blends franchised global brands with owned Indian concepts: Vaango (South Indian vegetarian cuisine) and The Food Street (food court format), plus Biryani By Kilo and Goila Butter Chicken acquired via Sky Gate Hospitality.
- The Chairman describes an organisational reset — a management bench strengthened under Manish, "The new team is fully in place now", building what the team calls "DIL 2.0", with continued confidence expressed by Yum! Brands in DIL and RJ Corp as long-term partners.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Merger] "The merger process with Sapphire Foods continues to progress along expected timelines. We received approvals from both the NSE and the BSE in June, bringing us closer to the next phase of regulatory filings. The timelines are broadly on track with our stated target of completion by the end of FY27."
- [Acquisition] "Acquired 105 Sky- Gate stores in June-25" (Q1 FY26 own-brand net new units of 105 reflect this), bringing Biryani By Kilo and Goila Butter Chicken into the portfolio.
- [Demand risk] "the forecast of a below-normal season, combined with El Niño risk, is a reminder that consumption recovery in India rarely moves in a straight line", with the operating environment described as volatile.
- [Governance] The presentation is signed by Pankaj Virmani, "Chief Sustainability Officer & Company Secretary" — the only sustainability-related reference in the document.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: Devyani delivered a strong Q4FY26 with KFC posting its best SSSG (4.9%) in 14 quarters driven by a strategic pivot to dine-in, while guiding for 200-225 net new stores in FY27. The proposed merger with Sapphire Foods remains on track for completion by FY26 end, promising scale synergies, though near-term margins face pressure from elevated coffee/cocoa costs and gas volatility.

open.item: Upon completion of the Sapphire Foods merger, the combined entity is expected to operate more than 3,000 stores globally.
The merged DIL-Sapphire entity is expected to generate approximately USD 1 billion in annual revenues.
Management flags that demand recovery is still evolving after a subdued discretionary spending environment through much of the year.
Strengthen the leadership team ahead of a significantly larger organisation, with new leadership under Mr. Manish Dawar and experienced professionals inducted across key functions.
Leverage digital platforms, data analytics, artificial intelligence and automation across operations to build a more agile, scalable and future-ready organisation (DIL 2.0).
Follow a balanced India expansion strategy based on increasing geographic penetration across Tier II and Tier III cities to maximise scale and brand synergies.
Pursue disciplined, cluster-based store expansion with leaner store formats optimised for the market environment, with calibrated KFC growth and Pizza Hut portfolio optimisation.
Focus on improving store economics, driving same-store sales growth and expanding margins through operational efficiencies.
Deepen presence in Tier II and Tier III cities in India while advancing the footprint in Thailand and Nepal, with KFC as the primary growth engine and Pizza Hut focused on portfolio rationalisation.
Build out the 'DIL Commerce' platform as the backbone of the Company's technology ambitions, giving a unified 360-degree view of customers across dine-in, takeaway and online channels.
Build India's leading integrated Food & Beverage platform through a multi-cuisine, multi-format 'House of Brands' portfolio spanning global and homegrown brands.
The merger is expected to unlock operational synergies estimated at 2-2.25 Billion in savings every year once integration is completed.

risks.note: Exposure to economic slowdowns, inflationary pressures and shifts in consumer sentiment that may adversely affect discretionary spending and overall demand. Mitigated through a multi-tier pricing architecture, continuous menu innovation and value engineering to offset input-cost inflation, and ongoing monitoring of macro indicators to recalibrate pricing and promotions. Management explicitly flags that near-term uncertainties relating to consumer demand and input costs will require close monitoring.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic & market risk - discretionary demand sensitivity

risks.note: Revenue volatility from festive cycles, regional demand patterns and evolving consumer preferences can hit store-level performance and capacity utilisation. Addressed with advanced analytics and predictive demand modelling, agile workforce and inventory planning, and targeted campaigns and product bundling to drive traffic in lean periods.

Process inefficiencies, execution gaps or dependency on key personnel may disrupt operations or impact service quality across a 2,000-plus store network. Mitigated by clearly defined standardised operating procedures across locations, a strengthened governance structure with defined roles, accountability and escalation mechanisms, and leadership pipeline development with structured succession planning.
risks.risk: Operational & organizational risk - execution and key-person dependency

risks.note: Supplier concentration, logistics constraints, geopolitical factors and commodity price volatility can affect availability and cost structures for a food business. Managed through a diversified, geographically distributed supplier network, long-term strategic sourcing agreements for cost predictability, technology-enabled supply-chain visibility with real-time inventory tracking, and periodic supplier audits and risk assessments.

Attracting, retaining and upskilling talent in a high-attrition industry can impact service delivery and growth plans; the BRSR shows permanent-employee turnover remaining elevated. Mitigated by structured recruitment, onboarding and performance management, continuous investment in training and leadership development, engagement and wellness programmes with performance-linked incentives, and a focus on diversity, equity and inclusion.
risks.risk: Human capital risk in a high-attrition industry

risks.note: As the business becomes increasingly technology-enabled - with digital ordering, kiosks, analytics and data-driven HR and supply-chain systems - risks relate to system downtime and scalability limitations, making resilience of digital platforms central to operations.

Identified in the BRSR double-materiality assessment as a material risk with negative financial implications: any compromise in food safety and quality may result in customer dissatisfaction along with regulatory scrutiny, notices and penalties. Mitigated through rigorous hygiene standards from preparation to storage under strict SOPs, regular evaluation of stores by franchisors, third-party agencies and regulators, and sourcing of all critical raw materials from GFSI-compliant suppliers.

BRSR-identified material risk with negative financial implications: inadequate waste management can result in regulatory non-compliance, and improper disposal may lead to environmental contamination of soil, water and air. Governed by the Company's Environment and Waste Management Policy covering waste reduction, segregation, timely disposal, hygiene standards and regulatory compliance.
